_comment: Template for state/config.json. Copy this file to ../state/config.json and fill it in during first-run enrollment (see SKILL.md). This file holds only acos-email-sort's own operational settings — folders, thresholds, delegate keywords. Identity/org-chart data (VIP list, signoff, partner vendors, protected contacts) now lives in the shared acos-aboutme skill; the fields below with the same names are a local fallback only, used when acos-aboutme isn't installed or a given list is empty there.
signature_first_name_note: Local fallback only — superseded by acos-aboutme's owner.signoff whenever that profile exists and has one set.
vip_senders_note: Local fallback only — superseded by acos-aboutme's vip_senders whenever that profile exists and is non-empty.
partner_vendors_note: Local fallback only — superseded by acos-aboutme's partner_vendors whenever that profile exists and is non-empty. A message from one of these domains is never auto-declined, even if it matches a template.
protected_senders_note: Local fallback only — superseded by acos-aboutme's protected_senders whenever that profile exists and is non-empty. A message from one of these addresses is never auto-declined, even if it matches a template.
internal_domain_note: Local fallback only — superseded by acos-aboutme's owner.email domain whenever that profile exists. Any sender on this domain always routes to 2_review (see find_internal_or_operational_alert in triage.py), skipping the bulk-mail and decline checks entirely. Also skips calendar/OOO artifacts (see calendar_ooo_note below) -- an internal sender's calendar accept/decline notice shouldn't be forced into 2_review with nothing to actually review.
ea_note: Local fallback only for ea_name/ea_email — superseded by acos-aboutme's staff entry whose role contains 'Executive Assistant' whenever that profile exists. ea_scheduling_keywords has no acos-aboutme equivalent and is always sourced from here. A message that mentions the EA by name (or the generic 'Executive Assistant' title) AND separately contains scheduling language routes straight to 3_delegate (see find_ea_scheduling_delegate in triage.py), skipping protected_contact/bulk/decline entirely. Every other delegate-worthy judgment stays an LLM call per delegate_keywords below.
operational_alert_senders_note: Exact sender-address matches for automated security/service-level alerts about your own systems (e.g. Microsoft Entra/PIM role-assignment notices, SharePoint storage warnings) that should always land in 2_review rather than being swept into 6_bulkToReview by the generic no-reply/ESP-padding bulk signature. Exact-address match only, not domain-wide, so a broad microsoft.com/google.com match doesn't sweep in unrelated marketing. Add entries as they turn up.
delegate_keywords_note: Confirm the real delegate-vs-review boundary with your EA before trusting this list. In this config's real-world example, the EA handles scheduling/calendar coordination and all travel logistics (including travel-related receipts/reimbursement), so those route to 3_delegate — but non-travel invoices/receipts (e.g. a software subscription) and general invoice/AP payment-request emails are the owner's own to handle, so they deliberately route elsewhere instead. Keep travel-specific phrasing (e.g. 'travel receipt') rather than bare 'receipt' or 'expense report' if your own delegate boundary is similarly travel-only — a bare 'receipt'/'reimbursement' keyword would delegate every invoice regardless of type.
priority_keyword_signals_note: Sender-independent positive priority signals, checked in score_priority alongside the existing VIP-sender/high-importance/urgent-keyword checks -- a genuine invoice, active deal document, or HR-lifecycle notice escalates to 1_priority even from a sender who isn't a VIP. All three are suppressed entirely for calendar/OOO subject artifacts, same as high-importance and urgent-keyword -- see calendar_ooo_note below (the VIP-sender signal itself is NOT suppressed for calendar/OOO artifacts).
accounts_payable_address_note: Not read by any deterministic check in triage.py -- this is reference data for the LLM's own judgment call during a live run (see SKILL.md's 'invoice, general AP payment request, or non-travel receipt' bullet under Judgment calls). When this address is already a recipient/cc on a message that financial_document_keyword_patterns escalates to 1_priority, the run-summary line for that message should note that AP is already in the loop -- a sign this is likely a quick review-then-file pass rather than one needing a payment action from the owner personally. Leave empty if there's no dedicated AP inbox to check for.
financial_document_excluded_senders_note: A small allowlist of known auto-pay-confirmation senders whose recurring, fully-automated 'invoice' notices need no review -- e.g. a subscription/spend-management service's automatic replenishment receipt, which is a record that a payment already happened, not a bill needing action. Only excludes the financial_document_keyword_patterns check for that sender, not deal_document or hr_lifecycle.
urgent_keyword_excluded_senders_note: Mirrors financial_document_excluded_senders -- a small allowlist for senders whose automated report titles reuse a status word (e.g. '...Approved') that reads as an approval keyword out of context but is just a trailing label, not a request. Scoped to only the urgent_keyword_patterns loop.
personal_action_request_keyword_patterns: A direct, personal ask that names you specifically and needs a reply only you can give -- keep these narrow and specific (a letter-of-recommendation request, a GitHub mention blocking a merge), not a broad category.
vendor_onboarding_keyword_patterns_note: Paired with a known partner_vendors name match in score_priority (not a standalone list) -- catches a vendor's own account-setup/invitation notice even when it arrives via an unrelated third-party platform. Deliberately requires BOTH the vendor name AND this onboarding language; a bare vendor-name mention alone (e.g. in a signature block) is not priority-worthy.
calendar_ooo_note: A subject starting with Automatic reply:, Accepted:, Declined:, Tentative:, or Canceled:/Cancelled: is an Outlook-generated calendar/OOO artifact, never a judgment call the sender made -- score_priority (see is_calendar_or_ooo_artifact in triage.py) suppresses the high-importance flag, the urgent-keyword scan, and the financial/deal/HR-lifecycle keyword scans for these. The VIP-sender signal is exempted from this suppression, but ONLY for genuine Automatic reply: messages (see is_calendar_rsvp_artifact) -- a VIP's pure calendar RSVP (Accepted:/Declined:/Tentative:/Canceled:) is still fully suppressed, since an RSVP is pure attendance metadata with no content, unlike an Automatic reply which can carry real content.
farewell_note_keyword_patterns_note: A one-time personal farewell/thank-you note from someone leaving shouldn't be escalated all the way to 1_priority the way the HR-lifecycle keywords above do, but it also shouldn't fall silently into 2_review with no distinguishing flag. Deliberately narrow phrasing -- a bare 'thank you' is far too common in ordinary business mail to use alone.
routine_notification_note: Two deliberately narrow, content-based (not sender-based) categories that route straight to 7_toBeFiled, ahead of find_protected_match: (1) meeting_reminder_keyword_patterns -- any meeting reminder is safe to file, no need to compare the referenced meeting time against the message's own received time; (2) routine_payroll_notification_keyword_patterns -- recurring payroll/task-tracking pings from a vendor like Rippling specifically, not a blanket sender rule. Keep these narrow enough that a notification actually asking you to do something (a missing-receipt request, a required-info request) still falls through to its normal path toward 2_review.
filed_without_action_threshold_note: Tracks a sender-behavior signal separate from decline_threshold above: a sender whose mail keeps reaching the 'routine, file it' judgment call and landing in 7_toBeFiled with no action taken. At this count in a run, add a run-summary recommendation to consider unsubscribing or creating a rule -- never anything more automatic than that note.
fallback_decline_topic_note: 4_autorespond doubles as a manual 'this is a decline' landing zone -- scripts/triage.py match-declines uses this topic for anything found there that doesn't match any template's own keywords. Must name a topic that actually exists in templates_file.
personnel_content_keyword_patterns_note: Checked in score_sensitive as an ADDITION to sensitive_keyword_patterns above, not a replacement -- catches personnel-adjacent content a general employee announces in plain language (a colleague's departure, a staff opening) regardless of sender domain, where sensitive_keyword_patterns only fires on messages that already sound like an HR-system notice. 'last day at <org>' should be edited to name your own organization. Avoid a bare 'accepted an invitation' style phrase here -- it collides with unrelated access-grant/invitation-acceptance notices (e.g. a third-party service confirming someone accepted a shared-account invite), which are a security signal, not a personnel one.
folder_naming_note: The live mailbox's fourth folder is named '4_autorespond' (not '4_autoresponse' as first drafted in the build spec) — this config reflects what actually exists. Rename either side if you want them to match; the skill works fine with either as long as this config's folder_names.autorespond value matches the real folder.
folder_restructure_note: '6_bulkToReview' is a screening lane for newsletter/bulk-send mail (see scripts/triage.py's is_bulk_or_newsletter) that sits ahead of the flat '7_toBeFiled' pile, giving a quick manual pass before final filing. Adjust the folder_names values here to whatever your own mailbox actually uses; this skill never creates folders itself.
